source_organisation_1: Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina (MoS BiH); Eurostat (ESS)

footer_fields.label: Reference metadata
footer_fields.value: Eurostat Metadata – SDG 10.60: Asylum applications by state of procedure

national_indicator_definition: The indicator presents the number of first-time applicants for international protection and the number of positive first-instance decisions on applications for international protection, expressed per million inhabitants. A first-time applicant for international protection is a person who lodges an asylum application for the first time in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Positive first-instance decisions are decisions taken by the competent authority acting as the first instance in the asylum procedure, granting international protection or another applicable form of protection in accordance with the relevant rules.
national_rationale: The indicator provides information on developments in the number of first-time applicants for international protection and positive first-instance decisions in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Monitoring these data contributes to understanding developments in the area of international protection and migration.
national_methodology_characteristics: The data for the indicator are based on national administrative data on international protection provided by the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina – Sector for Asylum. The Sector for Asylum is responsible for processing asylum applications, issuing decisions in asylum procedures, registering asylum seekers and maintaining official records and databases. For the purposes of SDG indicator 10.60, the data are presented in accordance with the Eurostat methodological framework and expressed as the number per million inhabitants. The indicator comprises two separate time series: first-time applicants for international protection and positive first-instance decisions. These two series do not represent the same group of persons in the same year, since an application submitted in one year may be decided in a later year. The data are collected from administrative records and processed in accordance with the requirements for internationally comparable statistics. The methodological definitions and rules for this indicator are aligned with the Eurostat methodology. Progress assessment is not applicable to this indicator under the EU SDG indicator methodology because no relevant policy target has been established against which progress could be assessed.
national_long_objective: No specific national target has been established for this indicator in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The indicator is used to monitor developments in the area of international protection through the number of first-time applicants and positive first-instance decisions per million inhabitants.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator shows the number of first-time applicants for international protection per million inhabitants and the number of positive first-instance decisions per million inhabitants. A first-time applicant for international protection is a person who lodged an application for asylum for the first time in the reporting country. First-instance decisions are decisions taken by the respective authority acting as a first instance in the administrative or judicial asylum procedure in the receiving country.
eu_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor developments in the area of international protection in the European Union. It provides information on the number of first-time applicants for international protection and positive first-instance decisions in relation to the population.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The data are based on administrative data on international protection supplied to Eurostat by national ministries of interior and related official agencies within the European Statistical System (ESS). Data on first-time applicants, first-instance decisions and population are used to calculate the indicator. Values are expressed as the number per million inhabitants. The indicator comprises two separate time series: first-time applicants for international protection and positive first-instance decisions. Caution is required when comparing these two values, since applications received in a given year might not be processed until a later year. The data are produced according to the quality standards of European Statistics and the methodological rules applied to statistics on international protection.
eu_long_objective: The indicator is used to monitor developments in the area of international protection within the EU SDG indicator set. No policy target has been established for this indicator against which progress could be assessed.
